s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute bilateral visual disturbance with transient visual obscurations and tinnitus, associated with optic disc edema and posterior fossa abnormalities
salient_findings: Bilateral blurry vision with transient visual obscurations
key_facts: Optic disc edema worse in the right eye
Disc hemorrhages and exudates in the right eye
Multiple cysts in the posterior fossa
Large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle

raw.syndrome_frame: Subacute bilateral visual disturbance with transient visual obscurations and tinnitus, associated with optic disc edema and posterior fossa abnormalities
salient_findings: Bilateral blurry vision with transient visual obscurations
key_facts: Optic disc edema worse in the right eye
Disc hemorrhages and exudates in the right eye
Multiple cysts in the posterior fossa
Large cyst at the level of the fourth ventricle

shortlist.label: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral optic disc edema and transient visual obscurations are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Arachnoid Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior fossa cysts and obstructive hydrocephalus are compatible with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior fossa abnormalities and obstructive hydrocephalus are features of this condition

shortlist.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension, this condition also presents with optic disc edema and visual disturbances

shortlist.label: Optic Neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral optic disc edema and visual disturbances could be related to this condition, although less likely given the posterior fossa findings

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bilateral blurry vision, transient visual obscurations, and bilateral optic disc edema are consistent with increased intracranial pressure, which is a hallmark of Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension. The presence of obstructive hydrocephalus due to the cysts could contribute to the increased pressure, and the normal CSF analysis supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Arachnoid Cyst
rejected.why: While the patient has an arachnoid cyst, it is unlikely to be the primary cause of the bilateral optic disc edema and visual symptoms.

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
rejected.why: This condition is typically diagnosed in infancy or early childhood and is characterized by hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle, which is not the primary finding in this case.

rejected.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
rejected.why: This is an older term for Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension, and the diagnosis is essentially the same.

rejected.label: Optic Neuritis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with unilateral optic disc edema and visual loss, which does not match the bilateral presentation in this case.
